_note: All wording is invented for this file. 'a' stands in for a published problem, restated here from public knowledge of famous puzzles or from a made-up problem. None of it comes from the corpus.

reskins.a: One hundred lockers are closed. Student k toggles every k-th locker, for k from 1 to 100. How many lockers end open?
reskins.b: A street has 625 porch lights, all off. Each of 625 volunteers walks past in turn, and volunteer j flips every j-th light. How many lights end up lit?

reskins.a: Find the minimum number of moves to transfer 8 discs between three pegs, never placing a larger disc on a smaller one.
reskins.b: A librarian shifts 6 books of different thickness between three carts, one at a time from the top, and a thicker book may not sit on a thinner one. What is the least number of shifts?

reskins.a: Find the sum of the integers from 1 to 100.
reskins.b: A pyramid of tins has 1 tin in the top row, 2 in the next, down to 60 in the bottom row. How many tins are there?

reskins.a: How many people must be in a room so that two certainly share a birth month?
reskins.b: How many socks must be pulled from a drawer of 7 colours to be sure of a matching pair?

reskins.a: Fifteen people sit in a circle and every second person is eliminated until one remains. Which starting seat survives?
reskins.b: Forty campers stand in a ring and every second camper leaves for the bus until only one is left. Which position stays last?

reskins.a: A rabbit population starts with one pair, and every pair produces a new pair each month from its second month. How many pairs are there after 12 months?
reskins.b: A climber goes up a 14-step staircase taking one or two steps at a time. In how many ways can the climb be done?

reskins.a: In how many ways can 8 non-attacking rooks be placed on a chessboard?
reskins.b: Seven pilots are each assigned to one of seven planes, one pilot per plane. How many assignments are there?

reskins.a: Letters are placed at random into addressed envelopes, 6 of each. In how many ways does no letter reach the right envelope?
reskins.b: Seven guests collect their coats so that nobody receives their own coat. How many ways can this happen?

reskins.a: How many ways can 2n people in a line be paired so that the pairing has no crossing arcs, for 2n = 10?
reskins.b: How many balanced strings of 6 opening and 6 closing brackets exist?

reskins.a: A wolf, a goat and a cabbage must cross a river in a boat that holds the farmer and one item. What is the least number of crossings?
reskins.b: A cat, a mouse and a wedge of cheese must be taken across a canal by a boatman who can carry only one at a time. How few trips are needed?

reskins.a: Twelve coins include one counterfeit that is heavier or lighter. What is the fewest weighings on a balance needed to find it?
reskins.b: A dozen identical pills include one of a different mass, heavier or lighter. How few uses of a two-pan scale will always identify it?

reskins.a: Two trains 150 km apart approach at 50 km/h each while a fly flies between them at 75 km/h until they meet. How far does the fly fly?
reskins.b: Two cyclists 60 km apart ride towards each other at 20 km/h each while a swallow shuttles between them at 45 km/h until they meet. What distance does the swallow cover?

reskins.a: Remove two opposite corners of a chessboard. Can the rest be tiled by dominoes? Answer with the number of tilings.
reskins.b: A 10 by 10 floor has two diagonally opposite tiles removed. How many ways can the remaining floor be covered with 1 by 2 mats?

reskins.a: A snail climbs 3 m up a 10 m wall each day and slips 2 m each night. On which day does it reach the top?
reskins.b: A hiker gains 5 km up a 26 km trail each day and slides back 4 km each night. On which day does the hiker reach the end of the trail?

reskins.a: A bat and ball cost 110 pence together, and the bat costs 100 pence more than the ball. What does the ball cost in pence?
reskins.b: A pen and a notebook cost 340 pence together, and the notebook costs 300 pence more than the pen. How much does the pen cost in pence?

reskins.a: A lily patch doubles in size daily and covers a lake on day 48. On which day did it cover half the lake?
reskins.b: A mould colony doubles daily and fills its dish on day 30. On which day was the dish half full?

reskins.a: Show how many handshakes occur when 20 people each shake hands once with everyone else.
reskins.b: In a round-robin league with 18 teams, each pair plays exactly once. How many matches are played?

reskins.a: How many squares of all sizes are on an 8 by 8 chessboard?
reskins.b: A 6 by 6 window has panes in a grid. How many square blocks of panes of any size can be outlined?

reskins.a: How many zeros does 100 factorial end with?
reskins.b: When 250 factorial is written out in full, how many trailing zeros does it have?

reskins.a: What is the probability that at least two of 23 people share a birthday?
reskins.b: On a planet with a 400-day year, what is the chance that at least two of 30 colonists share a birth date?

same_technique.a: Show how many integers must be chosen from 1 to 100 to guarantee two that differ by exactly 10.
same_technique.b: Among seven points in a unit hexagon, what is the smallest distance guaranteed between some pair?

same_technique.a: How many integers from 1 to 600 are divisible by none of 2, 3 or 5?
same_technique.b: How many surjections are there from a 6-element set to a 3-element set?

same_technique.a: How many binary strings of length 12 contain no three consecutive ones?
same_technique.b: A frog on a pentagon jumps to an adjacent vertex each second. In how many ways can it return to the start after 10 jumps?

same_technique.a: The roots of x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 are a, b, c. Find a^2 + b^2 + c^2.
same_technique.b: If p and q are the roots of x^2 - 5x + 2, find the quadratic whose roots are p/q and q/p.

same_technique.a: Find the last three digits of 7 to the power 2024.
same_technique.b: For how many n from 1 to 50 is 2^n + 3^n divisible by 5?

same_technique.a: Positive a, b, c have sum 3. Find the minimum of 1/a + 1/b + 1/c.
same_technique.b: Find the maximum of 2x + 3y + 6z when x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1.

same_technique.a: Two chords AB and CD meet at P inside a circle, with PA = 3, PB = 8 and PC = 4. Find PD.
same_technique.b: A tangent from T touches a circle at S, and a secant through T meets the circle at U and V. Given TU = 4 and UV = 5, find TS.

same_technique.a: A red die and a blue die are thrown together. Find the chance that red shows more than blue.
same_technique.b: How many subsets of a 10-element set have an even number of elements?

same_technique.a: How many solutions in non-negative integers does a + b + c + d = 20 have?
same_technique.b: In how many ways can 15 identical sweets go to 4 children if each child gets at least 2?

same_technique.a: How many integers from 1 to 1000 are a difference of two squares?
same_technique.b: Find all n for which n^2 + 60 is a perfect square, and give their sum.

same_technique.a: Evaluate the sum of 1/(k(k+1)) for k from 1 to 99.
same_technique.b: Find the product of (1 - 1/k^2) for k from 2 to 50.

same_technique.a: A rectangle has sides 6 and 8. Find the distance from a corner to the far diagonal.
same_technique.b: An equilateral triangle of side 2 has a point at distance 1 from two vertices. Find the distance to the third.

same_technique.a: A 2 m post casts a 3 m shadow at the moment a tree casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the tree?
same_technique.b: In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse splits it into parts 4 and 9. Find the altitude.

same_technique.a: In how many ways can 50 pence be made from coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 pence?
same_technique.b: How many partitions of 12 use only odd parts?

same_technique.a: Numbers 1 to 20 are on a board. Replace two numbers a, b by a + b - 1 repeatedly. What number remains at the end?
same_technique.b: Can a knight tour a 5 by 5 board starting on a black corner square and ending on a white square? Give 1 for yes, 0 for no.

same_technique.a: Each of 10 towns has one road to its nearest town, with all distances different. What is the most roads that can end at one town?
same_technique.b: Eleven real numbers have the property that each is the average of its two circular neighbours. How many distinct values can occur?

same_technique.a: How many distinct values does the floor of n^2/100 take for n from 1 to 100?
same_technique.b: Solve for x in the reals: floor(x) times x = 12, and give x as a fraction.
For how many n up to 100 is the fraction (n + 4)/(n + 11) in lowest terms?

same_technique.a: A random permutation of 1 to 10: what is the expected number of fixed points?
same_technique.b: Ten coins are tossed in a row. What is the expected number of runs of heads?

same_technique.a: ABC is isosceles with AB = AC and angle A = 20 degrees. Find the angle between the median from A and side AB.
same_technique.b: A cyclic quadrilateral has angles A = 80 and B = 110 degrees. Find angle C and angle D, and give their difference.
